references.text: The same materials (blue and purple wool, crimson thread, and fine linen) are mentioned as gifts for the tabernacle.
The same fabrics and skilled workmanship are used for the tabernacle curtains.
The breastpiece is made from the same materials as the ephod: gold, blue and purple wool, crimson thread, and woven fine linen.
Describes skilled women who spin blue and purple wool, crimson thread, and fine linen.
Fulfillment of the command to make the ephod with the specified materials.
Aaron is clothed in the ephod during his consecration as high priest.
The execution of the ephod confirms that God's command was followed exactly.
The resemblance of the breastpiece to the ephod emphasizes the theological unity of the priestly service.
The veil shares the same holy materials as the ephod, symbolizing the unity between the entrance to God's presence and the priestly service.
The belt's unity with the ephod shows that the priest's clothing is a complete symbol of obedience.
Gathering the specific materials is the necessary prerequisite for carrying out God's command regarding the ephod.
The robe's solid blue color contrasts with the multicolored weaving of the ephod and complements the picture of the priest's unified service.
The gate curtain shares the same holy materials as the ephod, showing the unity of the entire tabernacle structure.
Technical description of how gold was integrated into the same colors required for the ephod.
